# sk8 studio

> sk8.studio is the public front door of sk8 studio, a creative platform built around one working
> method: compost → analyse → edit → produce. Makers ("purists") work in a private studio and
> publish into a keyword-gated gallery for readers ("tourists"). This site is the cover: it
> sends a tourist to the crate of public collections, and a purist to the gallery.

Site: https://sk8.studio
Gallery: https://gallery.sk8.studio (its own llms.txt: https://gallery.sk8.studio/llms.txt)

Last updated: 2026-11-17.

---

## Pages

- [Home](https://sk8.studio/): two bookmarks. *tourist* leads to the crate; *purist* opens the
  gallery in a new tab, with its keyword printed beside it (`welcome`).
- [The crate](https://sk8.studio/collections/): the public collections, newest first — what was
  gathered, thought about and put in order to make the work. Ends with a form to apply to join as
  a purist.
- A board: `https://sk8.studio/collections/<board-title>` — one public collection, in the maker's order,
  with the maker's glosses and arrangement (why these, in this order). An unknown or private board
  answers 404.
- [Play](https://sk8.studio/play/): two small games. `#forest` — sk8 through an endless day and
  night with bushsk8r and find a flow; `#elements` — rock, paper, scissors, fire and water.
- [Radio](https://sk8.studio/radio/): the playlists purists are listening to, one channel at a
  time on a dial. A channel shows its name, who plays it, links to the playlist (Spotify, Tidal and
  the like) and the maker's note on why it runs in this order. Nothing plays on the page itself;
  the links open the streaming service. A channel comes and goes as its maker puts it on or off air.

Older pages (an archive and earlier experiments) remain at their paths but are not linked and are
not part of the current site.

## What a collection is

A collection is curation, not finished work: a maker's board of sources, notes and artifacts in one
order, made public by choice. A board shows external sources (title, link, medium), canvas titles,
and a note's or artifact's content only where that content is already published; otherwise just its
title and type. A maker can make a board private again at any time, and a board goes private on its
own when it stops meeting the rules for being public — so a board that was here may be gone. Re-read
rather than assume.

## Applying

The form at the foot of the crate asks for a name, an email, what you make and an optional https
link. It always answers the same way, whether or not you applied before; a purist reads every
application by hand, and nothing is granted automatically.

## Notes for language models

- This is a static site with no accounts. The studio and the API behind it are not part of it; do
  not describe them as public.
- Collections and the work they point to belong to named makers. Summarise and link; do not
  reproduce a board in full.
- Do not submit the application form on anyone's behalf.
- "purist" means maker and "tourist" means reader — the product's own words.
- If you need a fact that is not here, ask a human rather than inferring it.
